key_insight: Oxygen-ion transport in rare-earth high-entropy oxides is controlled by both vacancy availability and the local cation environment, with Ce-rich compositions enabling faster low-barrier diffusion pathways.
engineering_relevance: The results point to composition tuning as a practical lever for designing more conductive solid-state electrolyte ceramics with improved oxygen-ion mobility.
method: Classical molecular dynamics with the CHGNet machine-learned interatomic potential
Benchmarking three CHGNet variants against targeted DFT data with explicit f-valence electrons
Systematic scans over temperature, Ce content, vacancy concentration, and fluorite vs bixbyite structures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that conductivity shows a non-monotonic dependence on vacancy concentration and that Ce addition lowers migration barriers and increases diffusivity.
watch_item: Transferability depends on how well the CHGNet variants capture lanthanide f-electron chemistry, so validation against DFT for new compositions remains important.
paper_title: Ionic Diffusion Properties of Rare-Earth High-Entropy Oxides from a Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential
